Hi Soojin / Monica / Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited to move from eval to a reserved pool. I wanted to surface what we've scoped on our side so we can align on the activation runway and any gating items from Redwood.

High-level ask: a dedicated GPU pool for our image-generation model workload with predictable burst capability for batch runs (nightly reindex) and low-latency inference for interactive products.

Key constraints and preferences from Orchid:
- Primary region: us-east-1 (latency-sensitive dashboards). Secondary: eu-west-1 for EU customers.
- Expected steady-state QPS: ~120 requests/minute, 95th percentile latency target < 200ms for short prompts.
- Regular nightly batch jobs that require temporary +2x capacity for 2–3 hours daily (approx. 0200–0500 UTC).
- Compliance: SOC2 data handling questions are being collected by our security team (we’ll send a questionnaire next week).
- Contract: Procurement will push a standard PO; timeline target is to begin provisioning in early June.

Attached a short capacity sketch (orchid-reserve-mapping-v1.pdf) and our preferred SOW template. Can you confirm:
1) Recommended reserve size and burst strategy for these patterns?
2) Proposed warm/cold pool approach and expected warm-up times for kernel/kv cache for image models?
3) Any blockers from Dedicated activation or NetOps (VPC peering, egress rules)?

We'd like a short kickoff call to lock the rollout plan and milestone owners — available Wed/Thu this week.

Thanks,
Maria
Maria Gonzales
Head of Infrastructure, Orchid AI

Hi Maria — great to see the sketch, and thanks for the clear ask. I pulled together an initial activation plan and a concise action matrix to make the handoff to Ops and CS as frictionless as possible. See key points below; I’ve attached the activation-action-matrix.xlsx for owners and timelines.

Summary recommendation (short):
- Reserve: Start with a 16-GPU reserved pool (H100 class suggested, see Rishi's note below) to meet baseline interactive SLAs.
- Staging burst: Configure autoscale burst capacity of +8 GPUs (on-demand burst) with a 10% reserved headroom for safety (i.e., warm cache pool of ~2 GPUs).
- Staggered nightly batch window: Use scheduled burst policy 02:00–05:00 UTC with a hard upper limit of +32 GPUs for short windows if needed — this protects other tenants and gives Orchid predictability for cost.
- Warm pool behavior: Maintain a small warm pool (2–3 instances) for incoming interactive sessions to keep KV caches hot for common prefixes; cold-start for the rest. Expected 30–90s for a full warm-up depending on sequence lengths.

Operational asks from Redwood side:
- VPC peering & route tables: NetOps needs final CIDR and approved egress rules (security to confirm port ranges).
- Canary rollout: We'll do a phased canary (10% traffic -> 50% -> 100%) across the first 48 hours of go-live.
- SLOs & monitoring: CS will onboard Orchid into the per-route latency dashboard; we'll alert on token-level cost spikes and >5% error rate.

Proposed next steps / owners (from activation-action-matrix.xlsx):
- Redwood NetOps (Aditya) — VPC peering, egress, firewall rules — due 2026-05-20.
- Redwood Infra (Rishi) — cluster sizing, GPU class confirmation, quantization recommendations — due 2026-05-18.
- CS (Soojin) — kickoff, runbook, and stakeholder comms — due 2026-05-14.
- Orchid Procurement (Maria) — PO and SOW signoff — target 2026-05-25.

Can we lock a 30-min kickoff tomorrow at 10:30am PT? If not, Thursday works. I’ll include runbook excerpts and the burst policy matrix on the call.

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

Quick technical notes to refine the sizing and kernel choices before we finalize the SOW:

GPU class & sizing:
- For your image-generation models and the latency targets, H100s are recommended if you need consistent single-digit ms encoder ops; otherwise A100s (80GB) are a cost-effective baseline. If cost is a major concern start with A100 and reserve an option to upgrade to H100 during the nightly bursts.
- Suggested initial config: 8x A100 reserved + 8x burst-capable H100s on-demand (or 16x H100 reserved if budget allows). This lets you test warm/cold transitions without risking baseline latency.

Autoscale & burst policy specifics:
- Policy type: Scheduled burst with reactive headroom. Schedule nightly window 02:00–05:00 UTC; during that window allow reactive scaling to max cap for queued batch jobs. Outside the window, cap reactive bursts to +8 GPUs.
- Cooldown & pre-warm: Set a pre-warm trigger 10 minutes before scheduled runs (API hook or cron) to spin up warm pool. Cooldown of 20 minutes after batch completion to drain without overprovisioning.

Canary rollout & behavior:
- Canary traffic routing: We'll direct 10% of the US-East traffic to the dedicated pool for the first 12 hours; if 95p latency and error rate look good, increase to 50% then full cutover.
- KV cache strategy: Use prefix-aware caching for common prompts; full KV warm-up time can be parallelized across model shards. Expect 1–3 minutes for full cache for heavy image prompts unless pre-warmed.

Monitoring / SLOs to bake into the SOW:
- 95th percentile request latency (interactive) <200ms
- Batch job completion within agreed durations per job spec (to be defined by Orchid)
- Error rate <1% per 10-minute window during canary

I can prepare a short technical appendix to attach to the SOW describing warm-up timings, recommended kernel builds, and tuning knobs (quantization vs fp16/32 tradeoffs). Ping me if you want that attached.

- Rishi
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
